other_failure_modes.name: train_test_knn_skew
other_failure_modes.description: When constructing KNN distance features, the agent queries the training set against a tree built on the exact same training set. This causes the first nearest neighbor for training samples to always be the point itself (distance 0), while test samples have non-zero distances. This introduces a systematic train-test distribution skew.

other_failure_modes.name: unscaled_nn_target
other_failure_modes.description: The agent trains a neural network for regression without scaling the target variable. Since the target (capacity_mw) can have very large values, this can lead to massive gradients and unstable training with MSE loss.

other_failure_modes.name: cv_leakage_imputation
other_failure_modes.description: Missing values are imputed using the median of the entire training dataset before performing cross-validation splitting. This leaks the distribution of the validation folds into the training folds, slightly compromising the integrity of the cross-validation.

other_failure_modes.name: optimistic_oof_blending
other_failure_modes.description: The out-of-fold predictions used to optimize the ensemble blending weights are generated by models that use early stopping on those same validation folds. This makes the OOF predictions overly optimistic and can bias the meta-learner or blender.

summary: The solution is a well-structured pipeline using cross-validation and an optimized ensemble of LightGBM, XGBoost, CatBoost, and a PyTorch Neural Network. The agent correctly avoids peeking at test data for global transformations. However, there is a critical flaw in the spatial KNN feature engineering where querying the training data against itself includes self-distances of zero, creating a systematic train-test distribution skew. Additionally, there are minor data leakages in the cross-validation setup due to global imputation and using early-stopped OOF predictions for blending.
